newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra soars at open on newspaper report.
newsitem.headline: Astra soars at open on newspaper report.

text.p: Shares in Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer Astra International soared at the open on Friday on a newspaper report that a group to which President Suharto is linked was interested in purchasing a stake, brokers said.
Astra rose 6.34 percent to 3,775 rupiah at the open on a volume of 890,000 shares.
Timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan said in an interview with the Kompas newspaper that the Nusamba group he controls was interested in a stake in Astra for investment purposes.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.

"We don't have any shares in Astra. But then we have an obligation to maintain the value of funds that we hold, we always look to investing it in a profitable firm," Hasan was quoted as saying in the interview. "We see that Astra International is a good and wealthy company to invest in."
Hasan said some shareholders in Astra had been approached to see if they were willing to sell their stake but gave no details if any agreements had been reached.

Astra shares soared last month on newspaper reports that a takeover bid may be in progress but tapered off after tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna announced he had bought a 9.81 percent stake in the firm.
His PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna cigarette company then announced that a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake in Astra, giving Putera Sampoerna effectively the largest shareholding.
